newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open firmer amid U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open firmer amid U.S. gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger in quiet trade on Monday, amid gains in U.S. Treasuries, a rise in the Canadian dollar and steady interest from domestic accounts, traders said.

"The U.S. market touched firmer too. I think we're tracking the U.S. a little, but there has been obviously some buying in our market because we're definitely trading with a decent bid right now," said one bond trader with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.52 to C$117.58 to yield 6.639 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 10/32 to yield of 6.60 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to four basis points from five basis points at Friday's close.
"I get the sense it's probably domestic (buying)," said one corporate bond trader with a Canadian bank. "It's pretty light trading."

Traders said activity in the Canadian market was quiet after the U.S. holiday weekend, when many Canadian market players left early. Analysts said the Canadian market had also begun to feel the effects of the traditional summer slowdown.

The Canadian dollar's holding of recent gains helped strengthen bond prices, traders said. The Canadian dollar opened flat at C$1.3735 (US$0.7280) in heavy trading on Monday after recovering from overnight weakness in overseas markets.

In economic news, the value of Canadian building permits issued in May fell 12 percent from April, Statistics Canada said. Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month decline of 0.1 percent in May. The data did not have a major impact on the market, dealers said.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.30 to C$108.83 to yield 6.037 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which firmed 7/32 to yield 6.28 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 24 basis points from 21 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.03 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.12 percent.
